title: Validate a Proposed Task Order
statement: You run a build pipeline with n tasks labeled 0 to n-1. You are given a list of dependency edges, where each edge [a, b] means task a must finish before task b starts. A teammate hands you a proposed order: a list of task labels describing the sequence in which they plan to run the tasks. Return True if the proposed order is a valid execution order, and False otherwise. To be valid, the order must list each of the n tasks exactly once (no task missing, no task duplicated, no label outside 0..n-1), and for every edge [a, b], task a must appear somewhere before task b in the order. An empty order is valid only when n is 0. Return a boolean.
hints: You do not need to build the ordering yourself here; you only need to check a candidate. What single fact about each task lets you compare two tasks' relative order in O(1)?

Record each task's index in the proposed order as a position map, but first confirm the order is a true permutation of 0..n-1 (right length, no duplicates, no out-of-range labels) so every edge endpoint is guaranteed present.

Reject early if len(order) != n. Then walk the order building pos[task] = i, returning False on any duplicate or out-of-range label. Finally, for each edge [a, b], return False if pos[a] >= pos[b]; if all edges pass, return True.
